title: Accept and read Krisis decision documents
summary: Accept immutable Krisis documents in one explicitly identified decisions library and read complete accepted text through its bounded feed.
use_when: Krisis must hand a document to its configured Annals decisions library.
A local consumer must freeze or page the accepted-document prefix with complete text.
do_not_use_when: General source material should enter the primary Annals inbox.
A caller wants to review, rank, supersede, retract, delete, or determine the current force of a decision.
The decisions-library config and exact expected persistent library ID are unavailable.
outcome: One durable producer acceptance and unstarted inbox job, an exact idempotent replay, or a bounded immutable feed view fixed to a requested watermark.
effects: First acceptance copies unchanged document bytes into a producer-identified inbox envelope and appends one immutable acceptance row.

A decision-config inbox run binds only a fresh empty spool or verifies its existing binding, ignores ordinary incoming files, and dispatches only committed producer-accepted originals or their explicit retry children.
Exact replay and feed reads are side-effect free; conflicting bytes, invalid input, maintenance, insufficient storage, or identity mismatch create no acceptance.
Acceptance starts no source delivery, model run, reconciliation, or corpus transition; later inbox dispatch retains its separate existing effects.
authority: Krisis owns decision identification, document construction, and the producer key. No document content schema is required by Annals.
Annals owns library and spool identity, accepted bytes, producer idempotency, job identity, event order, and supported accepted-content access.
A feed event records acceptance of a document, not successful interpretation or enactment of a decision.
success: A created or replayed receipt identifies contract version, exact library, producer, key, SHA-256, stable original job, and acceptance time without content or paths.
A page echoes the requested watermark and cursor, returns ascending immutable events, and leaves an empty-page cursor unchanged.
Concurrent identical calls converge on one acceptance and concurrent different-byte calls have at most one winner.
failure_and_recovery: Retry an ambiguous acceptance only with the identical producer key and bytes; never mint a replacement key because dispatch failed.
If envelope publication completed before an uncertain database commit, the next identical call reconstructs the acceptance from that envelope.
Stop on missing or mismatched config, schema, library identity, spool identity, envelope, or digest. Do not redirect or edit receipts.
privacy: Complete documents remain private in producer handoff state and Annals spool, library, archives, and backups. Later model dispatch may disclose document and library context under the inbox contract.
Feed output includes complete document text, which can include full normalized conversation. Keep it private and out of routine logs. It excludes general-library content.

interfaces.label: Accept into a named decisions library

does_not_authorize: Release, installation, provisioning, migration, activation, historical import, publication, remote sharing, direct SQLite or spool editing, deletion, pruning, or storage cleanup.
Using the primary library, changing the configured target per account, or treating local producer routing as authentication against the local user.
Consumer acknowledgement, correction, retraction, review, confidence, disposition, supersession, relationship, semantic relevance, or current-force state.

consumers.statement: Krisis may submit immutable text documents; local consumers may read the resulting accepted-document prefix.

preconditions.statement: Every exchange command names an explicit decisions config or a registered decisions name whose managed config binds a library, inbox root, and exact 32-lowercase-hex expected library ID. The current schema, persistent identity, and immutable decisions role must match. Acceptance or dispatch binds or verifies spool identity.
New acceptance additionally requires no deployment maintenance and enough spool headroom to preserve the configured reserve.

inputs.statement: Acceptance takes producer krisis, a trimmed nonblank single-line key of at most 512 bytes, and one regular non-symlink nonblank UTF-8 text file of at most 1 MiB. Accessible text is sufficient; no extension, headings, content schema, source metadata, source lookup, or fitness check is required.
A page takes one committed watermark, one earlier watermark or item cursor, and a limit from 1 through 200.

decision-feed start takes the same explicit library selection and returns a Watermark-shaped opaque cursor before the first acceptance. Use it as page --after to read existing documents without a retained consumer cursor.

outputs.statement: Acceptance JSON reports contract_version, library_id, producer, key, source_sha256, job_id, accepted_at, and acceptance created or replayed.
Watermark JSON reports contract and library identity plus an opaque token. Pages echo library, watermark, request_cursor and next_cursor and return complete accepted-document events.

data_semantics.statement: Producer acceptance means Annals durably owns one exact complete spool copy and the immutable producer tuple. Source delivery, processing, reconciliation, and corpus application have separate records.

Each event supplies cursor, event_id, document_id equal to the producer key, source_name, source_sha256, accepted_at, and document containing exact unchanged UTF-8 text. Filename and normal storage metadata come from the file and Annals, not required document fields.

identity_and_units.statement: Producer idempotency is scoped by persistent library ID, immutable decisions role, producer krisis, and producer key; SHA-256 binds exact bytes, job ID binds the original queue item, and event and cursor values are opaque.
accepted_at describes Annals acceptance, not occurrence of a decision. SHA-256 identifies exact document bytes. File and page content bounds count UTF-8 bytes; the event limit counts records.
accepted_at is an RFC3339 timestamp of Annals acceptance.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: A watermark freezes every committed acceptance through one sequence; pages return the ascending prefix strictly after the requested cursor and no later than that watermark.

The feed includes accepted documents before dispatch and after later processing success or failure. It supplies no historical Decisions rows, unaccepted records, dispatch result, semantic interpretation, correction, retraction, or consumer acknowledgement.

access.statement: Named scope is an identity-checked wrapper over the same account/feed command. Operator-path calls still require explicit --config and reject --library. A name or librarian instruction change cannot bypass immutable decisions admission.
The supported boundary is the local Annals CLI with an explicit decisions config or registered identity-bound decisions name; acceptance permits only producer krisis and feed commands are read-only.

With decision_feed configured, Annals rejects direct work add or integration, generic enqueue, ordinary incoming registration, and backlog import. The decisions database rejects these routes through any config, spool, or direct selector. Dispatch permits accepted originals and explicit retry children.
Library override, environment or frontend fallback, direct SQLite access, receipt editing, cross-library query, and remote access are unsupported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: First acceptance publishes one complete unstarted envelope, then commits its event. Exact replay returns the original result. Changed bytes conflict without mutation. Recovery resolves publication uncertainty from the envelope.
Pages are fixed to one watermark, strictly ascending, replay a committed prefix after uncertainty, and preserve the exact request cursor when empty; Annals keeps no consumer cursor.

operational_limits.statement: A file is at most 1 MiB. A page request selects 1 through 200 events, with at most 4 MiB of document bytes excluding JSON and transport fields. Short nonempty pages may continue; only empty pages end the fixed prefix. New spool copies preserve the configured available-byte reserve.
No acceptance, queue, dispatch, model, storage, schedule, throughput, quality, or wall-clock service-level objective is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Exchange contract 2, library schema 7, producer receipt 1, feed cursor 1, provider release, and later inbox/Nucleus protocols are separate axes. Documents have no content schema version. Migration preserves original sequences, IDs, digests, jobs, times, and cursor meaning; old projections remain historical.
Changed accepted bytes, correction, retraction, or a new event type cannot be introduced under this exchange identity.

reliances.statement: Acceptance and feed reads invoke no Conversations, Nucleus, Clockwork, model, network, or remote service; later dispatch has its own declared Nucleus reliance.
